newsitem.title: HUNGARY: U.S. Defense Secretary Cohen arrives in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Defense Secretary Cohen arrives in Hungary.

text.p: United States Defense Secretary William Cohen arrived in Hungary on Wednesday as part of a diplomatic blitz of Central and Eastern Europe by U.S. officials in the wake of the Madrid NATO summit.

Cohen, President Bill Clinton and Secretary of State Madeleine Albright are fanning out across the region to explain U.S. policy on expansion of NATO after the 16 alliance members agreed on Tuesday in the Spanish capital to invite Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic to become new members.
Clinton is spending Thursday in Poland and will travel to Romania on Friday morning.
Albright will accompany Clinton to Warsaw and Bucharest and then take her own tour of Slovenia, Russia, the Baltic States and the Czech Republic.

"It is logical that Secretary Cohen would come here because we have American troops stationed in Hungary and as Secretary of Defense those trooops are his responsibility," the U.S. Budapest Embassy spokeswoman Susan Elbow told Reuters.
Hungary is the only former Warsaw Pact state playing host to a U.S. army base, at Taszar, southern Hungary, which acts as a logistical staging post for U.S. peacekeeping operations in Bosnia.

After meeting Hungarian presdent Arpad Goncz, Prime Minister Gyula Horn and the country's defence and foreign ministers on Thursday morning, Cohen will address a 200-strong audience of politicians and dignitaries in Hungary's parliament before flying down to Taszar in the afternoon.
Elbow added that Cohen, on his first visit to Hungary since taking over as Defense Secretary from William Perry, would express U.S.pleasure that Hungary had made the first group of new NATO members.
However another embassy source said Cohen would also spell out in his speech some of Hungary's obligations as a new NATO member.

"There'll be a little bit about 'hard work still ahead'," the source said. "He'll say 'It's not all over and done, you've got to finish your (civilian controls), you've got to be more NATO compatible, you've got to modernise, we want you to close the gap between yourselves and the other NATO members'."

On Friday Cohen will fly to Lviv in Ukraine to attend military peacekeeping exercises with Ukrainian, Russian and U.S. troops before flying on to Kiev, where he plans to meet President Leonid Kuchma and other officials on Saturday.
On Sunday he will fly to Sofia for meetings with Bulgarian President Petar Stoyanov and other officials and leaves for Washington on Monday.
